title: Fractures and suspected dislocations
description: A broken bone or a joint that has come out of place after a fall, blow, or twist.

recognition_questions.q: Is there pain, swelling, or an unnatural angle at the site of injury?
Can the person move the limb, or is it too painful?
Is the bone visible through the skin, or is there a wound near the break?

observable_symptoms: Numbness or coldness beyond the injury
immediate_safety_warnings: Do not try to push the bone back into place.
Do not move the person if you suspect a spine, neck, or pelvic injury unless they are in danger.

ordered_instructions.instruction: Keep the person still and support the injured limb in the position you found it.
Call 112 if the fracture is open (bone visible), or involves the neck, spine, pelvis, or a major leg bone, or if the person is in severe pain.
For an open fracture, control bleeding with a clean cloth around the wound, but do not press directly on the bone.
ordered_instructions.rationale: Bleeding control without pushing bone back.

ordered_instructions.instruction: Immobilise the limb with a splint or by padding around it and supporting it. Do not move it to apply the splint.
Apply a cold compress wrapped in cloth to reduce swelling.
Check the fingers or toes beyond the injury for warmth, colour, and feeling. If cold, pale, or numb, the limb needs urgent attention.

actions_to_avoid: Do not try to reduce (push back) a dislocation or fracture.
Do not move the limb to test it.
Do not give food or drink (surgery may be needed).
Do not apply the splint so tight it cuts off circulation.

escalation_conditions.action: Call 112; control bleeding; risk of infection
Call 112; do not move; keep still

escalation_conditions.condition: Limb is cold, pale, or numb beyond the injury
escalation_conditions.action: Urgent hospital care; blood supply at risk

escalation_conditions.condition: Severe pain, deformity, or the person cannot move

equipment_requirements.item: Splint (rigid material: stick, board, rolled magazine)
Bandages or cloth strips to tie the splint

approved_alternatives.alternative: Rolled newspaper/magazine, stick, umbrella rib, folded cardboard
A piece of cloth tied around the neck to support an arm

follow_up_requirements: All suspected fractures need an X-ray and medical assessment.
Re-check circulation and feeling in the limb regularly until treated.

age_specific_pathways.child: Children's bones are more flexible — greenstick fractures can be subtle. Seek assessment for any significant injury.
age_specific_pathways.infant: Any suspected fracture needs urgent assessment; do not move unnecessarily.

source_references.document: International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines
